answer: Texas uses electronic titles, so the lender sends the lien release to the state electronically rather than on paper, and there's no paper title to bring to your appointment. If the title still shows the bank as lienholder, the lien hasn't been released yet, so ask your lender to release it. If that doesn't work, you can sign the lien release request (form NW-LRL-1) and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. We can still make you an offer and book your appointment while you wait.
